acts.title: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
acts.short_description: Comprehensive law to prevent atrocities against members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, providing special courts, victim rights, relief and rehabilitation.
acts.plain_language_summary: This law provides special protections for individuals from SC/ST communities against atrocities, discrimination, and violence. It establishes fast-track Special Courts, guarantees victim and witness protection, mandates immediate financial relief/compensation, and ensures free legal aid.
applicable_incident_categories: Caste discrimination, physical assault and threats
acts.official_source_name: India Code · Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice

key_provisions.title: Rights of Victims and Witnesses
key_provisions.summary: Guarantees rights to protection from intimidation, regular updates on case proceedings, free legal aid, travel/maintenance allowance during hearings, and protection from harassment.

key_provisions.title: Special Courts & Exclusive Special Courts
key_provisions.summary: Mandates speedy trial and disposal of atrocity cases within two months of filing the chargesheet wherever feasible.

acts.title: Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
acts.short_description: Prescribes punishment for the preaching and practice of 'Untouchability' and for the enforcement of any disability arising therefrom.
acts.plain_language_summary: This Act makes it an offence to deny any individual access to public places, water bodies, religious premises, employment, or community services on grounds of untouchability or caste-based discrimination.
applicable_incident_categories: Discrimination, public humiliation and employment exclusion
acts.official_source_name: India Code · Ministry of Law and Justice

acts.title: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
acts.short_description: Constitutes legal services authorities to provide free and competent legal services to the weaker sections of the society.
acts.plain_language_summary: Under Section 12 of this Act, victims of caste atrocities, women, children, persons with disabilities, and individuals in custody are entitled to free legal aid, legal representation, and payment of court fees through NALSA, SLSAs, and DLSAs.

acts.title: Victim Rights and Relief Provisions under Indian Law
acts.short_description: Statutory provisions governing victim compensation, recording of statements by female police officers, and medical examination.
acts.plain_language_summary: Indian criminal procedure guarantees that survivors of violence are entitled to free medical treatment at all hospitals, prompt FIR registration, sensitive statement recording, and application to the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) for interim victim compensation.
acts.official_source_name: Department of Justice · Ministry of Law and Justice

rights.title: Right to Protection & Safety
rights.summary: Protection from threats, coercion, inducements, violence or intimidation by the accused or their associates.
rights.details: Under the SC/ST PoA Act (Section 15A) and Witness Protection Schemes, police and district administration are legally mandated to evaluate threat perceptions, provide physical security or police escort, and protect survivors and witnesses throughout the legal process.

rights.title: Right to Free Legal Aid & Counsel
rights.summary: Complete free legal representation from filing the complaint through appeals.
rights.details: Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act guarantees that eligible survivors pay zero fees for legal counsel, drafting petitions, court appearances, certified copies, and witness travel expenses through NALSA and DLSA panels.
rights.source: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 Section 12 · NALSA

rights.title: Right to Information on Proceedings
rights.summary: Timely information regarding court dates, bail hearings, chargesheet filing, and verdicts.
rights.details: Survivors and legal heirs have the right to be notified about all court dates, summons, bail applications moved by the accused, chargesheet submissions, and trial proceedings with reasonable advance notice.

rights.title: Right to Relief & Financial Compensation
rights.summary: Mandated financial relief and interim compensation disbursed at stage milestones.
rights.details: Under the PoA Rules (Schedule Annexure I) and Central/State Victim Compensation Schemes, survivors are entitled to mandated relief amounts. A portion is disbursed immediately upon FIR registration, chargesheet, and court conviction to cover immediate medical, legal, and survival needs.
rights.source: PoA Rules 1995 (Schedule Annexure I) · DoSJE / NALSA

rights.title: Right to Dignified & Sensitive Treatment
rights.summary: Trauma-informed treatment free from discriminatory or humiliating practices.
rights.details: All police, medical, and judicial officers are required by law to conduct examinations and proceedings with dignity. Recording of statements for women and minors must be done in a safe environment by female officers wherever available.
rights.source: Ministry of Home Affairs & Supreme Court Guidelines

process_stages.title: Case Registration & Intake
process_stages.general_overview: The complaint is formally received and assigned an official docket identifier. Initial police verification or FIR registration commences.
key_rights: Right to receive a free copy of the registered First Information Report (FIR).
Immediate referral to medical care and initial safety screening.
Option to request free legal aid from DLSA immediately.
process_stages.next_steps_overview: The investigating agency begins collecting evidence, recording statements, and filing preliminary paperwork.

process_stages.title: Police Investigation & Evidence Gathering
process_stages.general_overview: The appointed Investigating Officer (IO) collects forensic/documentary evidence, visits the scene, records witness statements, and determines whether an arrest is warranted.
key_rights: Protection from threats or coercion by accused parties (Section 15A PoA Act).
Statement recording in a safe and supportive setting.
Initial installment of statutory interim relief / victim compensation upon FIR.
process_stages.next_steps_overview: Upon completing investigation, the IO submits a final report or Chargesheet to the jurisdictional court.

process_stages.title: Court Hearings & Judicial Proceedings
process_stages.general_overview: The Special Court or District Court examines evidence, hears prosecution and defence arguments, and examines witnesses.
key_rights: Right to advance notification of all hearing dates and bail petitions.
Right to be accompanied by a legal aid advocate or support counsellor.
Travel, food, and daily maintenance allowance for attending court hearings.
In-camera proceedings or screen protection during sensitive testimony if requested.
process_stages.next_steps_overview: After witness examinations and final arguments, the court pronounces judgment and orders sentencing/final relief.

process_stages.title: Financial Relief Assessment & Disbursal
process_stages.general_overview: The District Magistrate / Nodal Agency / DLSA processes statutory financial relief according to prescribed legal schedules.
key_rights: Disbursal of balance relief compensation directly into survivor's bank account.
Reimbursement of medical and relocation expenses where applicable under state rules.
process_stages.next_steps_overview: Review of full disbursal and transition into long-term rehabilitation support.

process_stages.title: Long-Term Rehabilitation & Social Support
process_stages.general_overview: Support measures to assist the survivor in regaining emotional stability, vocational security, education, and safe housing.
key_rights: Access to government vocational training and livelihood support schemes.
Assistance with educational admission or safe housing if relocated.
Continued psychosocial support sessions with assigned counsellors.
process_stages.next_steps_overview: Ongoing monitoring by Safe Circle and community support network.

legal_aid.title: Free Legal Aid & Legal Services Authorities
legal_aid.authority: National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) & State/District Legal Services Authorities (SLSA/DLSA)
legal_aid.statutory_basis: Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
legal_aid.eligibility_summary: Free legal aid is guaranteed by law to: (1) Members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, (2) Women and children, (3) Victims of trafficking or beggar, (4) Persons with disabilities, (5) Victims of mass disaster, ethnic violence, or atrocity, and (6) Persons in custody.
services_covered: Payment of court fees, process fees, and all other charges payable in proceedings.
Providing service of lawyers in legal proceedings (Civil, Criminal, Revenue, Appellate).
Obtaining and supplying certified copies of orders and other documents in legal proceedings.
Preparation of appeal, paper book including printing and translation of documents in legal proceedings.

faqs.question: What is free legal aid and who pays for my lawyer?
faqs.answer: Under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, free legal aid means the government through NALSA or the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) provides an experienced advocate without any fees from you. Court fees, typing, and paper costs are also covered.
faqs.official_source: NALSA Legal Services Authority Act Section 12

faqs.question: What can I do if I or my family feel unsafe or face intimidation?
faqs.answer: Under Section 15A of the SC/ST PoA Act and the National Witness Protection Scheme, you have a legal right to state protection. You can notify your Investigating Officer, Special Court, or District Nodal Officer immediately. SAATH can also alert your assigned counsellor to assist in filing a protection requisition.

faqs.question: How does victim compensation and financial relief work?
faqs.answer: Relief is disbursed in standardized installments at different milestones (upon FIR, upon chargesheet submission, and upon court decision). Disbursal is ordered by the District Magistrate or DLSA directly to your bank account without requiring application fees.
faqs.official_source: PoA Rules 1995 & Central Victim Compensation Scheme

faqs.question: What happens during court trials in a Special Court?
faqs.answer: Special Courts are designated fast-track courts established to hear atrocity cases with sensitivity and speed. You have the right to a free legal aid advocate, advance notice of dates, travel allowances, and in-camera protection if safety is a concern.

faqs.question: Is the information provided here considered legal advice?
faqs.answer: No. SAATH provides educational and supportive summaries sourced from official government statutes. It does not replace an advocate or provide binding legal conclusions. For decisions specific to your case, please consult your assigned DLSA legal counsel.
